description: Machine-readable ethics/security/privacy/quality/compliance rules enforced across every tool in this repository. Human rationale lives in docs/POLICY.md. Each rule has a stable diagnostic code; the validation package (packages/validation) implements the checks. 'enforcement: automated' rules are checked by code; 'enforcement: attested' rules are confirmed via SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md and reviewed. Critical (blocking) rules cannot be suppressed locally.

categories.structure: Required files, native manifest schema, naming
categories.version: Single authoritative version source and cross-manifest consistency
categories.disclosure: Honest disclosure of capabilities, permissions, side effects, limitations
categories.security: Secure defaults, secrets, injection, path safety, install boundaries
categories.ethics: No deceptive, harmful, or unauthorized behavior
categories.quality: Meaningful validation/tests; no placeholders or false success
categories.compliance: Conformance to the current official platform specification

rules.summary: Tool has a manifest/tool.json with required fields (name, type, targets, version, license).
rules.remediation: Add manifest/tool.json with the required metadata block.

rules.summary: Tool name is kebab-case, unique, no spaces or special characters.
rules.remediation: Rename the tool to kebab-case.

rules.summary: Claude plugin has .claude-plugin/plugin.json with a valid name; components live at plugin root, not inside .claude-plugin/.
rules.remediation: Move components to plugin root; keep only plugin.json in .claude-plugin/.

rules.summary: Skill has a SKILL.md with name and description frontmatter.
rules.remediation: Add SKILL.md with required frontmatter.

rules.summary: Cursor rule is a .mdc file with valid frontmatter (description/globs/alwaysApply).
rules.remediation: Provide a .mdc rule with valid frontmatter.

rules.summary: Placement matches targets: single-host tools live under tools/<host>/, multi-host under tools/portable/.
rules.remediation: Move the tool to the correct directory for its declared targets.

rules.summary: Referenced files, scripts, and assets exist at the declared relative paths.
rules.remediation: Fix or remove broken references.

rules.summary: No path traverses outside the plugin root (../); plugins are self-contained (Claude requirement).
rules.remediation: Bundle the referenced content or use a plugin dependency instead of an external path.

rules.summary: Exactly one authoritative version source (package.json); native manifests are stamped from it, not hand-maintained.
rules.remediation: Set the version only in package.json; let packaging stamp the native manifest.

rules.summary: Version is valid SemVer and consistent across all manifests.
rules.remediation: Align the version across package.json and native manifests.

rules.summary: Breaking security/privacy/permission/compatibility changes are not shipped in a patch release.
rules.remediation: Use a minor/major bump and document the breaking change.

rules.summary: Manifest declares capabilities: filesystem read/write, shell, network, git, external APIs, MCP, credentials, telemetry, remote content.
rules.remediation: Fill in the capabilities/disclosure block in manifest/tool.json.

rules.summary: README documents purpose, limitations, supported platforms, required permissions, side effects, and destructive operations.
rules.remediation: Complete the README disclosure sections.

rules.summary: No unsupported evidence-free labels (secure, safe, verified, validated, compatible, portable, tested, production-ready) without backing.
rules.remediation: Remove or substantiate the claim.

rules.summary: A declared target host is only listed after its validator + fixture pass; no unverified compatibility claims.
rules.remediation: Remove the target or add passing verification for it.

rules.summary: No committed secrets, private keys, tokens, or .env files containing values.
rules.remediation: Remove the secret and rotate it; use .env.example placeholders.

rules.summary: No install-time remote code execution (e.g. curl|bash) from untrusted sources.
rules.remediation: Vendor the content or require HTTPS + pinned version + integrity check + explicit user action.

rules.summary: No unsafe shell construction or command injection; inputs are validated/quoted.
rules.remediation: Quote variables, validate inputs, avoid eval.

rules.summary: No path traversal or unsafe symlinks in tool content or package.
rules.remediation: Constrain paths to the tool/package root.

rules.summary: Portable paths only: use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/host variables, never hardcoded absolute or home paths.
rules.remediation: Replace absolute/~ paths with the provided environment variables.

rules.summary: install.sh/validate.sh detect the platform before touching the filesystem and write only to declared, scoped targets.
rules.remediation: Source scripts/lib/detect-platform.sh and scope writes.

rules.summary: Requests the minimum necessary permissions; no permission overreach inferred from category.
rules.remediation: Declare and justify each permission explicitly.

rules.summary: Collects/reads/transmits only data required for the declared operation (data minimization).
rules.remediation: Remove unnecessary data access; document what remains.

rules.summary: No sensitive content in logs, diagnostics, telemetry, handoff files, or release artifacts.
rules.remediation: Redact sensitive fields; keep them out of outputs.

rules.summary: Any external transmission is intentional, documented, authorized, and minimal.
rules.remediation: Document and gate the transmission, or remove it.

rules.summary: Tool does not mislead users, hide side effects, fabricate evidence, exfiltrate data, weaken security, or conceal vulnerabilities.
rules.remediation: Redesign the tool to comply; generation/validation fails otherwise.

rules.summary: No destructive or remote-system changes without explicit user authorization; dry-run/preview offered where practical.
rules.remediation: Gate consequential actions behind explicit authorization and previews.

rules.summary: Dual-use security tools clearly distinguish defensive/authorized use and required authorization.
rules.remediation: Add scope, authorization, and prohibited-use documentation.

rules.summary: Respects licenses, copyright, and attribution; no unlicensed redistribution; official docs not copied verbatim.
rules.remediation: Use compatible sources and write original content.

rules.summary: No placeholder lifecycle targets; no target returns success without meaningful execution.
rules.remediation: Implement the target or remove it.

rules.summary: Meaningful tests exist; disabled tests are not presented as passing.
rules.remediation: Add real tests; do not skip-and-pass.

rules.summary: Errors are actionable: non-zero exit, affected project/file, explanation, recommended action.
rules.remediation: Improve diagnostics to be actionable.

rules.summary: Declares the official specification/doc used for validation and the documentation review date.
rules.remediation: Add specSource and specReviewedOn to manifest/tool.json.

rules.summary: No speculative/invented native manifest fields; no cross-platform convention copied without official support.
rules.remediation: Remove unsupported fields; follow the target's official spec.

rules.summary: Package contains only tool-required files + metadata + license + integrity checksum; no monorepo, caches, temp, secrets, or machine paths.
rules.remediation: Fix the assemble step to include only required files.

rules.summary: Packaging is deterministic (stable ordering/paths) and produces a verifiable checksum.
rules.remediation: Normalize ordering/paths and emit a checksum.

rules.summary: validate-package inspects the final artifact (not just source) for prohibited files and manifest/version consistency.
rules.remediation: Run validate-package against the built artifact.

rules.summary: install writes only the selected tool to the selected scope; validates the package first; reports changed paths; fails safely (no partial install).
rules.remediation: Scope and validate the install; back up on overwrite.

rules.summary: uninstall removes only files owned by the tool; never user files or another tool's shared resources; supports dry-run.
rules.remediation: Track owned files and scope removal.

rules.summary: verify-install independently confirms installed files, version match, integrity, and no undeclared files.
rules.remediation: Implement verify-install checks.
